previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of chronic constipation, cerebrovascular accident with aphasia and quadriplegia, type 2 diabetes, and dysphagia was admitted after failing colonoscopy prep due to abdominal distension. Imaging showed marked colonic dilation without obstruction, free air, or ischemia. He remained asymptomatic with no pain, nausea, or vomiting. A colonoscopy was attempted but incomplete due to tortuous anatomy and poor prep. A virtual colonoscopy was performed, showing no obstructing mass. He was managed with bowel evacuation, continued PEG tube feeding, and medication adjustments, including temporary hold of anticoagulants. He was discharged to extended care with a stable condition, restart of warfarin and Plavix, bowel regimen including Miralax and Golytely, and follow-up on imaging results.

radiology_notes.text:
AP PORTABLE CHEST, ___, AT 1528 HOURS.

HISTORY:  Hypertension and intubation.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, the most recent dated ___.

FINDINGS:  Consistent with the given history, an endotracheal tube has been
introduced with the distal tip approximately 4 cm from the carina in
appropriate position.  Nasogastric tube extends off the inferior aspect of the
radiograph in the left upper quadrant with the sidehole projecting over the
gastric fundus.  Lung volumes are markedly diminished with hazy opacity in
bilateral lung bases, particularly on the left.  The aorta is mildly tortuous.
The cardiac silhouette size is grossly within normal limits accounting for
patient and technical factors.  No definite effusion or pneumothorax is noted.
The visualized osseous structures reveal degenerative changes throughout the
thoracic spine.

IMPRESSION:  Endotracheal and (presumed) nasogastric tubes in satisfactory
position. Hypoventilatory changes likely in the left lung base, although an
early developing pneumonia or aspiration cannot be excluded.  Correlate
clinically.

INDICATION:  History of CVA with altered mental status and hypotension, query
bleed.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast head CT.

There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage, shift of normally midline
structures, edema, hydrocephalus, or loss of gray-white matter junction
differentiation.  A left middle cranial fossa CSF-attenuation focus,
likely arachnoid cyst, persists. There is calcification of the vessels at the
base of the brain again seen. Osseous structures are grossly unremarkable,
mastoid air cells are clear. There is a small retention cyst in the left
maxillary sinus and mild ethmoidal mucosal thickening.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute intracranial process.

2.  Persistent left middle cranial fossa arachnoid cyst.

3.  Persistent vascular calcifications.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Followup.

COMPARISON:  ___, 3:28 p.m.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, a right-sided central
venous access line has been inserted over the internal jugular vein.  The tip
of the catheter projects over the superior vena cava.  The other monitoring
and support devices are unchanged.  Also unchanged is the size of the cardiac
silhouette.  No evidence of pneumothorax, no focal parenchymal opacity
suggestive of pneumonia.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Hypotension, followup.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, there is no relevant
change.  There is increased transparency of the right lung base with just a
minimal plate-like atelectasis.  Unchanged monitoring and support devices.  No
newly appeared focal parenchymal opacity suggestive of pneumonia.

HISTORY:  PICC line placement.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the earlier study of this date, the left PICC
line extends to the upper portion of the SVC.  Decreased lung volumes. 
Nasogastric tube and endotracheal tube have been removed.

INDICATION:  ___ male with hypertension.

COMPARISON:  CXR ___.

AP CHEST:  Right internal jugular central venous line and left PIC catheter
are unchanged.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is stable with persistent
tortuosity of the thoracic aorta observed.  Retrocardiac opacity may represent
atelectasis, and there may be a small left pleural effusion.  No significant
right pleural effusion or consolidation is seen.  There is no pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION: Persistent retrocardiac atelectasis with possible small left
effusion.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Followup of a patient with pneumonia.

Portable AP chest radiograph was compared to ___ obtained at
06:48 a.m.

The right internal jugular line is at the junction of brachiocephalic vein and
SVC.  The left PICC line tip is in mid SVC.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette
is unchanged.  Bilateral pleural effusions are present.  There is a slight
interval worsening in the right lower lobe opacity that might represent
progression of pneumonia.  No pneumothorax is demonstrated.
